decisions.decision: 240 Static/Static Calculation records are direct/deterministic candidates; 40 Complex and 17 Dynamic are deferred; 16 Physical Test records are evidence-only.

decisions.decision: Evidence/approval nodes use Draft, Submitted, UnderReview, Approved, Rejected, Expired, or Revoked plus authority, issue date, validity, scope, and provenance.
decisions.rationale: Boolean approval flags are inadequate for engineering assurance.

decisions.decision: Accept exact DNV/QUDT/W3C mappings only when the exact code or URI is independently verified; otherwise coin a benchmark term and retain aliases/provenance.
decisions.rationale: Prevents plausible but false ontology mappings.

decisions.decision: Use the current active workbook SHA-256 05eb02... as the file identity; retain 216885... only as unresolved legacy provenance metadata, not as publication identity.
decisions.rationale: The current file is directly hash-verifiable.

decisions.decision: Every shortlisted term must record its naming basis, authority, applied rule, original aliases, and QA result. A DNV mapping is never inferred from similar wording.
decisions.rationale: Makes each coined or reused name explainable in the paper and auditable later.

decisions.decision: Promote a readable canonical name only when the regulation defines the symbol or the locked variable already supplies a descriptive expansion. Preserve the symbol as an alias; otherwise do not create a canonical term solely from the symbol.
decisions.rationale: Eliminates opaque identifiers without inventing engineering meaning.

namingRules.application: Reuse an existing term only after exact URI/local-name and semantic-context verification.
namingRules.paperDefense: Prevents local-name-only matches across incompatible namespaces.

namingRules.application: Use the definition stated in the applicable clause; keep the original equation symbol as an alias.
namingRules.paperDefense: Improves readability without changing the regulated meaning.

namingRules.application: Remove units from local names and record unit, quantity kind, and verified unit URI separately.
namingRules.paperDefense: The same property remains stable across compatible unit representations.

namingRules.application: Normalize a descriptive locked variable to ASCII lowerCamelCase while preserving the original label as an alias.
namingRules.paperDefense: Provides typeable identifiers with direct provenance to the locked extraction.

namingRules.application: When no verified reusable term exists, coin subject/component + characteristic + qualifier/state from the verified clause.
namingRules.paperDefense: The construction rule is deterministic, readable, and does not imply a false external mapping.

namingRules.application: Spell separators as Point or Dash and name the governing instrument explicitly where a rule reference is itself data.
namingRules.paperDefense: Avoids ambiguous digit concatenations such as 111 or generic labels such as term2Status.

namingRules.application: Leave DNV, QUDT, W3C, Haitham, Rana, or AnchorMap mappings empty unless the exact identifier and meaning were verified.
namingRules.paperDefense: Avoids mapping hallucinations and keeps provenance auditable.

requirements.section: Maximum and minimum draught fore and aft
requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.sourceText: The ship shall always be loaded down at least to the draught of LIWL amidships when navigating in ice. Any ballast tank, situated above the LIWL and needed to load down the ship to this water line, shall be equipped with devices to prevent the water from freezing. In determining the LIWL, regard shall be paid to the need to ensure a reasonable degree of ice-going capability in ballast. The highest point of the propeller shall be submerged and if possible at a depth of at least h_i below the water surface in all loading conditions. The forward draught shall be at least (2 + 0.00025*Delta)*h_i [m], but need not exceed 4*h_i (2.1), where Delta is the displacement of the ship [t] determined from the waterline on the UIWL (see section 2.1). Where multiple waterlines are used for determining the UIWL, the displacement must be determined from the waterline corresponding to the greatest displacement. h_i is the level ice thickness [m] according to section 4.2.1.

requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF construction_stage_date >= '2003-09-01' AND iceClass IN {'IA Super','IA','IB','IC'}, THEN compute P_min = K_e*(R_CH/1000)^(3/2)/D_p at UIWL and LIWL; use draught-dependent inputs at the corresponding draught, use L and B at UIWL for both calculations, and require mcrPower_kW >= max(P_min_UIWL_kW, P_min_LIWL_kW). K_e shall be selected from Table 3-1. Table 3-1 values for conventional propulsion systems: 1 propeller: CP propeller or electric or hydraulic propulsion machinery 2.03, FP propeller 2.26; 2 propellers: 1.44 and 1.60; 3 propellers: 1.18 and 1.31.
requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.sourceText: To qualify for ice class IA Super, IA, IB or IC, a ship the keel of which is laid or which is at a similar stage of construction on or after 1 September 2003 shall comply with the following requirements regarding its engine output. The engine output requirement shall be calculated for two draughts by formula 3.1. Draughts to be used are the maximum draught amidships referred to as UIWL and the minimum draught amidships referred to as LIWL, as defined in section 2.2. In the calculations, the ship's parameters which depend on the draught must be determined at the appropriate draught, but L and B must be determined only at the UIWL. The engine output shall be no less than the greater of these two outputs. P_min = K_e*(R_CH/1000)^(3/2)/D_p [kW] (3.1), where K_e shall be given a value according to Table 3-1. The pressure to be used is 1.8p where p is determined according to 4.2.2. The load patch must be applied at locations where the capacity of the structure under the combined effects of bending and shear is minimised. In particular, the structure must be checked with a load centred at the UIWL, 0.5h0 below the LIWL, and positioned at several vertical locations in between. Furthermore, if the load length la cannot be determined directly from the arrangement of the structure, several values of la shall be checked using corresponding values for ca.

requirements.sourceText: Delta is the displacement of the ship at a maximum ice class draught [t] (see section 2.2). P is the actual continuous engine output of the ship [kW] (see section 3.1) available when sailing in ice. If additional power sources are available for propulsion power (e.g. shaft motors) in addition to the power of the main engine(s), they shall also be included in the total engine output used as the basis for hull scantling calculations. The engine output used for the calculation of the hull scantlings shall be clearly stated on the shell expansion drawing. cp is a factor that reflects the magnitude of the load expected in the hull area in question relative to the bow area. The value of cp is given in Table 4-3. ca is a factor which takes account of the probability that the full length of the area under consideration will be under pressure at the same time. It is calculated using the formula: l (4.4) ca = l0 , maximum 1.0, minimum 0.35, l0 = 0.6 m. a Values of la are given in Table 4-4. po is the nominal ice pressure; the value 5.6 MPa shall be used.

IF weather_deck_below_ice_belt_upper_limit = true, THEN bulwark_strength_status and freeing_port_strength_status shall meet the ice-belt shell requirement. The lower-speed model-test sentence is advisory and is not encoded as a mandatory constraint.
requirements.section: Vertical extension of ice strengthening for plating (ice belt)
requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.sourceText: In addition, the following areas shall be strengthened: Fore foot: For ice class IA Super, the shell plating below the ice belt from the stem to a position five main frame spacings abaft of the point where the bow profile departs from the keel line shall be ice-strengthened in the same way as the bow region. Upper bow ice belt: For ice classes IA Super and IA on ships with an open water service speed equal to or exceeding 18 knots, the shell plate from the upper limit of the ice belt to 2 m above it and from the stem to a position at least 0.2 L abaft of the forward perpendicular shall be ice-strengthened in the same way as the midbody region. A similar strengthening of the bow region is also advisable for a ship with a lower service speed when, on the basis of the model tests, for example, it is evident that the ship will have a high bow wave. Sidescuttles shall not be situated in the ice belt. If the weather deck on any part of the ship is situated below the upper limit of the ice belt (e.g. in the way of the well of a raised quarter decker), the bulwark shall be provided with at least the same strength as is required for the shell in the ice belt. The strength of the construction of the freeing ports shall meet the same requirements.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.sourceText: The aim of time domain torsional vibration simulations is to estimate the extreme torsional load for the ship's lifespan. The simulation model can be taken from the normal lumped mass elastic torsional vibration model, including damping. For a time domain analysis, the model should include the ice excitation at the propeller, other relevant excitations and the mean torques provided by the prime mover and hydrodynamic mean torque in the propeller. The calculations should cover variation of phase between the ice excitation and prime mover excitation. This is extremely relevant to propulsion lines with directly driven combustion engines. Time domain calculations shall be calculated for the MCR condition, MCR bollard conditions and for resonant speed, so that the resonant vibration responses can be obtained. For frequency domain calculations, the load should be estimated as a Fourier component analysis of the continuous sequence of half sine load sequences. First and second order blade components should be used for excitation.

requirements.section: Sea inlet and cooling water systems
requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.sourceText: For this purpose, at least one cooling water inlet chest shall be arranged as follows: 1. The sea inlet shall be situated near the centreline of the ship and well aft, if possible. 2. Guidance for designing the volume of the chest shall be around one cubic metre for every 750 kW in engine output of the ship, including the output of auxiliary engines necessary for the operation of the ship. 3. The chest shall be sufficiently high to allow ice to accumulate above the inlet pipe. 4. A pipe for discharge cooling water, allowing full capacity discharge, shall be connected to the chest. 5. The open area of the strainer plates shall be no less than four (4) times the inlet pipe sectional area. If there are difficulties in meeting the requirements of paragraphs 2 and 3 above, two smaller chests may be arranged for alternating the intake and discharge of cooling water. Otherwise, the arrangements and situation shall be as above. Heating coils may be installed in the upper part of the sea chest.

requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: The Manual shall include or refer to specific procedures to be followed in the event of incidents in polar waters.

requirements.sourceText: In order to comply with the functional requirements in section 2.2, the Manual shall be carried on board.

requirements.requiredInputs: Applicability flag and PWOM methodology section
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: In order to comply with the functional requirements of paragraph 2.2.2, the Manual shall contain, where applicable, the methodology used to determine capabilities and limitations in ice.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: PWOM risk-procedure coverage flags
requirements.canonicalVariables: PWOM_risk_procedure_coverage, voyage_limit_avoidance, environmental_forecast_arrangements, information_limitation_measures, required_equipment_operation, environmental_functionality_measures
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: PWOM shall include risk-based procedures covering voyage-limit avoidance, environmental forecasts, information limitations, required-equipment operation, and applicable low-temperature, topside-icing, and sea-ice functionality measures.
requirements.requiredInputs: PWOM and five required procedure coverage indicators
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: The Manual shall include risk-based procedures for the following: voyage planning to avoid ice and/or temperatures that exceed the ship's design capabilities or limitations; arrangements for receiving forecasts of the environmental conditions; means of addressing any limitations of the hydrographic, meteorological and navigational information available; operation of equipment required under other chapters of this Code; and implementation of special measures to maintain equipment and system functionality under low temperatures, topside icing and the presence of sea ice, as applicable.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: emergency_provider_contact_procedure_present, prolonged_entrapment_procedure_present
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: PWOM shall include applicable emergency-provider contact procedures; IF ship_ice_strengthened = true, THEN PWOM shall also include prolonged-ice-entrapment life-support and integrity procedures.
requirements.requiredInputs: PWOM, emergency-contact procedure, ice-strengthening status, and entrapment procedure
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: The Manual shall include risk-based procedures to be followed for: contacting emergency response providers for salvage, search and rescue (SAR), spill response, etc., as applicable; and, in the case of ships ice strengthened in accordance with chapter 3, procedures for maintaining life support and ship integrity in the event of prolonged entrapment by ice.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: exceedance_response_procedure_present
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: PWOM shall include procedures for encounters with ice or temperatures exceeding ship design capabilities or limitations.
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: The Manual shall include risk-based procedures to be followed for measures to be taken in the event of encountering ice and/or temperatures which exceed the ship's design capabilities or limitations.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: ice operation and escort procedure properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF ice_operation_applicable = true, THEN PWOM shall include ice-operation monitoring and safety procedures, including applicable escort or icebreaker-assistance requirements and operating-mode-specific limitations.
requirements.requiredInputs: PWOM, operation mode, escort requirements, and applicable limitations
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: The Manual shall include risk-based procedures for monitoring and maintaining safety during operations in ice, as applicable, including any requirements for escort operations or icebreaker assistance. Different operational limitations may apply depending on whether the ship is operating independently or with icebreaker escort. Where appropriate, the PWOM should specify both options.

requirements.sourceText: Materials of exposed structures in ships shall be approved by the Administration, or a recognized organization accepted by it, taking into account standards acceptable to the Organization or other standards offering an equivalent level of safety based on the polar service temperature.

requirements.requiredInputs: Ship category, ice-strengthening status, scantling approval, and standard evidence
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Scantlings of category A ships shall be approved by the Administration, or a recognized organization accepted by it, taking into account standards acceptable to the Organization or other standards offering an equivalent level of safety; scantlings of category B ships shall be approved by the Administration, or a recognized organization accepted by it, taking into account standards acceptable to the Organization or other standards offering an equivalent level of safety; and scantlings of ice strengthened category C ships shall be approved by the Administration, or a recognized organization accepted by it, taking into account acceptable standards adequate for the ice types and concentrations encountered in the area of operation.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: icing allowance and projected-area variables
requirements.canonicalVariables: ice_accretion_likely, deck_icing_allowance_kg_m2, side_icing_allowance_kg_m2, continuous_surface_projected_area, discontinuous_surface_projected_area, continuous_surface_static_moment, discontinuous_surface_static_moment
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF ice_accretion_likely = true, THEN deck_icing_allowance_kg_m2 = 30, side_icing_allowance_kg_m2 = 7.5, discontinuous_surface_projected_area = continuous_surface_projected_area * 1.05, and discontinuous_surface_static_moment = continuous_surface_static_moment * 1.10.
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: For ships operating in areas and during periods where ice accretion is likely to occur, the following icing allowance shall be made in the stability calculations: 30 kg/m^2 on exposed weather decks and gangways; 7.5 kg/m^2 for the projected lateral area of each side of the ship above the water plane; and the projected lateral area of discontinuous surfaces of rail, sundry booms, spars (except masts) and rigging of ships having no sails and the projected lateral area of other small objects shall be computed by increasing the total projected area of continuous surfaces by 5% and the static moments of this area by 10%.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: ice_accretion_likely and ice-removal properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF ice_accretion_likely = true, THEN ice_accretion_minimization_design_present = true AND required_ice_removal_means_present = true.
requirements.requiredInputs: Operating-area assessment, design evidence, and required ice-removal equipment inventory
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Ships operating in areas and during periods where ice accretion is likely to occur shall be: designed to minimize the accretion of ice; and equipped with such means for removing ice as the Administration may require; for example, electrical and pneumatic devices, and/or special tools such as axes or wooden clubs for removing ice from bulwarks, rails and erections.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: PWOM_icing_allowance_information_present and icing allowance values
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015

requirements.requiredInputs: PWOM and stability-calculation icing allowance values
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Information on the icing allowance included in the stability calculations shall be given in the PWOM.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: ice accretion monitoring and corrective-action variables
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: ice_accretion_monitoring_active = true; for every monitoring observation, observed_ice_accretion <= PWOM_ice_accretion_limit, or a linked corrective_action_status shall show action taken.
requirements.requiredInputs: Time-stamped ice-accretion observations, PWOM limits, and corrective-action records
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Ice accretion shall be monitored and appropriate measures taken to ensure that the ice accretion does not exceed the values given in the PWOM.

requirements.anchorMapField: iceClass -> reg:iceClass; No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: construction_date, residual_stability_factor_s_i and alternative compliance properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF ship_category IN {'A','B'} AND construction_date >= '2017-01-01', THEN for every applicable loading condition either residual_stability_factor_s_i = 1 or, where the SOLAS II-1/4.1 alternative applies, alternative_instrument_residual_stability_status = compliant.
requirements.requiredInputs: Ship category, construction date, loading conditions, calculated s_i, and alternative-instrument evidence
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Ships of categories A and B, constructed on or after 1 January 2017, shall be able to withstand flooding resulting from hull penetration due to ice impact. The residual stability following ice damage shall be such that the factor s_i, as defined in SOLAS regulations II-1/7-2.2 and II-1/7-2.3, is equal to one for all loading conditions used to calculate the attained subdivision index in SOLAS regulation II-1/7. However, for cargo ships that comply with subdivision and damage stability regulations in another instrument developed by the Organization, as provided by SOLAS regulation II-1/4.1, the residual stability criteria of that instrument shall be met for each loading condition.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: ice damage extent and position variables
requirements.canonicalVariables: upper_ice_waterline_length, damage_center_forward_of_max_breadth, longitudinal_damage_extent, transverse_penetration_mm, upper_ice_waterline_draught, vertical_damage_extent, allowed_vertical_position
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: longitudinal_damage_extent = 0.045 * upper_ice_waterline_length when damage_center_forward_of_max_breadth = true, otherwise 0.015 * upper_ice_waterline_length; transverse_penetration_mm = 760; vertical_damage_extent = min(0.20 * upper_ice_waterline_draught, longitudinal_damage_extent); allowed_vertical_position is between keel and 1.20 * upper_ice_waterline_draught.
requirements.requiredInputs: Damage scenario geometry and calculated extents
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: The ice damage extents to be assumed when demonstrating compliance with paragraph 4.3.2.1 shall be such that: the longitudinal extent is 4.5% of the upper ice waterline length if centred forward of the maximum breadth on the upper ice waterline, and 1.5% of upper ice waterline length otherwise, and shall be assumed at any longitudinal position along the ship's length; the transverse penetration extent is 760 mm, measured normal to the shell over the full extent of the damage; and the vertical extent is the lesser of 20% of the upper ice waterline draught or the longitudinal extent, and shall be assumed at any vertical position between the keel and 120% of the upper ice waterline draught.

requirements.sourceText: Fire pumps, including emergency fire pumps, water mist and water spray pumps, shall be located in compartments maintained above freezing.

requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: Every exposed fire-main section shall have isolation_capability = true AND drainage_means_present = true.
requirements.requiredInputs: Fire-main section inventory and isolation/drainage arrangements
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: The fire main is to be arranged so that exposed sections can be isolated and means of draining of exposed sections shall be provided.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: firefighter_outfit, storage_location_temperature_class
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: Every firefighter_outfit shall be stored in a location classified as warm.
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Firefighter's outfits shall be stored in warm locations on the ship.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: fixed-water-system and sea-suction properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF fixed_water_system_separate_from_main_fire_pumps = true AND independent_sea_suction_used = true, THEN sea_suction_ice_clearing_capability = true.
requirements.requiredInputs: System layout, suction configuration, and ice-clearing arrangement
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Where fixed water-based firefighting systems are located in a space separate from the main fire pumps and use their own independent sea suction, this sea suction shall also be capable of being cleared of ice accumulation.

requirements.activeStatus: Evidence-only - physical result not inferred by SHACL
requirements.anchorMapField: testTemperature_degC -> mat:testTemperature_degC; No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: extinguisher and freezing-protection/test properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.encodingPattern: Conditional location and environmental test constraint
requirements.normalizedRequirement: Every portable or semi-portable extinguisher shall be in a freezing-protected location; IF storage_location_subject_to_freezing = true, THEN extinguisher_operating_test_temperature_degC <= PST_degC AND operating_test_status = passed.
requirements.requiredInputs: Extinguisher inventory, location status, protection, and PST test evidence
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Portable and semi-portable extinguishers shall be located in positions protected from freezing temperatures, as far as practical. Locations subject to freezing are to be provided with extinguishers capable of operation at the PST.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: exposed_escape_route and safety/accessibility properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: Every exposed escape route shall have accessible_status = true, safe_status = true, and documented ice/snow mitigation coverage.
requirements.requiredInputs: Escape-route inventory, inspection status, and ice/snow mitigation evidence
requirements.section: Part I-A Chapter 8 - Escape and evacuation
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Exposed escape routes shall remain accessible and safe, taking into consideration the potential icing of structures and snow accumulation.

requirements.activeStatus: Evidence-only - physical result not inferred by SHACL
requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: life-saving appliance and evacuation-test properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: Every life-saving appliance and associated equipment item shall have evacuation_test_status = passed under applicable adverse conditions for demonstrated_duration_days >= maximum_expected_rescue_time_days.
requirements.requiredInputs: Appliance inventory, adverse-condition test records, and rescue-time requirement
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: All life-saving appliances and associated equipment shall provide safe evacuation and be functional under the possible adverse environmental conditions during the maximum expected time of rescue.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: person thermal-protection and environmental-coverage properties
requirements.canonicalVariables: person_on_board, assigned_thermal_protection, thermal_protection_approval_status, intended_voyage, anticipated_cold, anticipated_wind, immersion_potential
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: Every person on board shall have assigned thermal-protection equipment supported by an adequacy approval covering intended voyage, anticipated cold and wind, and applicable polar-water immersion.
requirements.requiredInputs: Persons-on-board manifest, assigned equipment, and adequacy evidence
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Adequate thermal protection shall be provided for all persons on board, taking into account the intended voyage, the anticipated weather conditions (cold and wind) and the potential for immersion in polar water, where applicable.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: survival-resource duration and coverage properties
requirements.canonicalVariables: abandonment_environment, survival_support_duration_days, maximum_expected_rescue_time_days, habitable_environment_present, weather_protection_present, accommodation_space_present, sustenance_means_present, safe_access_exit_present, rescue_communication_present
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: Survival resources shall support the assessed abandonment environments for at least maximum_expected_rescue_time_days and shall cover habitable environment, cold/wind/sun protection, accommodation space, sustenance, safe access/exit, and rescue communication.
requirements.requiredInputs: Operational assessment, survival-resource inventory, duration evidence, and six coverage indicators
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Taking into account the presence of any hazards, as identified in the assessment in chapter 1, resources shall be provided to support survival following abandoning ship, whether to the water, to ice or to land, for the maximum expected time of rescue. These resources shall provide: a habitable environment; protection of persons from the effects of cold, wind and sun; space to accommodate persons equipped with thermal protection adequate for the environment; means to provide sustenance; safe access and exit points; and means to communicate with rescue assets.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: ship_exposed_to_ice_accretion and protected-item properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF ship_exposed_to_ice_accretion = true, THEN every escape route, muster station, embarkation area, survival craft, launching appliance, and survival-craft access shall have an associated ice_or_snow_removal_or_prevention_means.
requirements.requiredInputs: Applicability assessment, protected-item inventory, and associated anti-icing means
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: For ships exposed to ice accretion, means shall be provided to remove or prevent ice and snow accretion from escape routes, muster stations, embarkation areas, survival craft, their launching appliances and access to survival craft.

requirements.activeStatus: Evidence-only - physical result not inferred by SHACL
requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: construction_date, exposed_escape_route, polar_clothing_passage_test_status
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF construction_date >= '2017-01-01', THEN every exposed escape route shall have polar_clothing_passage_test_status = passed.
requirements.requiredInputs: Construction date, route inventory, and representative passage-test evidence
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: For ships constructed on or after 1 January 2017, exposed escape routes shall be arranged so as not to hinder passage by persons wearing suitable polar clothing.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: ice-covered operation and evacuation properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF ship_operates_in_ice_covered_waters = true OR direct_evacuation_onto_ice_applicable = true, THEN safe_evacuation_means_present = true AND survival_equipment_deployment_approval_status = approved.
requirements.requiredInputs: Operating condition, evacuation arrangement, and deployment evidence
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Ships shall have means to ensure safe evacuation of persons, including safe deployment of survival equipment, when operating in ice-covered waters, or directly onto the ice, as applicable.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: added-device power and independence properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF added_life_saving_device_requires_power = true, THEN device_power_source_independent_of_main_power = true.
requirements.requiredInputs: Device inventory, power requirement, and power-source topology
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Where the regulations of this chapter are achieved by means of adding devices requiring a source of power, this source shall be able to operate independently of the ship's main source of power.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: person and assigned survival-equipment properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF ship_type = passenger_ship, THEN every person on board shall have one properly sized immersion suit OR one thermal protective aid.
requirements.requiredInputs: Ship type, persons-on-board manifest, equipment assignments, and size compatibility
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: For passenger ships, a proper sized immersion suit or a thermal protective aid shall be provided for each person on board.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: immersion_suit_required, immersion_suit_type
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF immersion_suit_required = true, THEN immersion_suit_type = insulated.
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Where immersion suits are required, they shall be of the insulated type.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: extended_darkness_operation, lifeboat, searchlight suitability properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF extended_darkness_operation = true, THEN every lifeboat shall have an assigned searchlight with continuous_use_suitability_status = approved.
requirements.requiredInputs: Operating profile, lifeboat inventory, searchlight assignment, and suitability evidence
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: For ships intended to operate in extended periods of darkness, searchlights suitable for continuous use to facilitate identification of ice shall be provided for each lifeboat.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: lifeboat, lifeboat_type
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: Every lifeboat_type shall be in {'partially enclosed','totally enclosed'}.
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: No lifeboat shall be of any type other than partially or totally enclosed.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: abandonment potential and group-survival equipment properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF abandonment_onto_ice_or_land_potential = true, THEN group_survival_equipment_carried = true OR normal_life_saving_equivalent_functionality_approval_status = approved.
requirements.requiredInputs: Operational assessment, group-equipment inventory, and equivalence approval evidence
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Whenever the assessment identifies a potential of abandonment onto ice or land, group survival equipment shall be carried, unless an equivalent level of functionality for survival is provided by the ship's normal life-saving appliances.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: survival-equipment capacity and storage properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF personal_or_group_survival_equipment_required = true, THEN available_survival_equipment_capacity >= ceil(persons_on_board * 1.10) AND storage_accessibility_status = accessible.
requirements.requiredInputs: Persons-on-board count, equipment capacity, and storage-location evidence
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: When required, personal and group survival equipment sufficient for 110% of the persons on board shall be stowed in easily accessible locations, as close as practical to the muster or embarkation stations.

requirements.activeStatus: Evidence-only - physical result not inferred by SHACL
requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: group-survival container test properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: Every group-survival-equipment container shall have ice_mobility_test_status = passed AND flotation_test_status = passed.
requirements.requiredInputs: Container inventory, ice-mobility test, and flotation test records
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Containers for group survival equipment shall be designed to be easily movable over the ice and be floatable.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: survival-craft and launching-appliance capacity variables
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF additional_equipment_carried_in_survival_craft = true, THEN survival_craft_available_capacity >= persons_capacity_requirement + additional_equipment_capacity_requirement AND launching_appliance_capacity >= loaded_survival_craft_requirement.
requirements.requiredInputs: Survival-craft loading calculation and launching-appliance capacity evidence
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: If carried in addition to persons, in the survival craft, the survival craft and launching appliances shall have sufficient capacity to accommodate the additional equipment.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: passenger instruction and crew training status properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: Every passenger shall have personal-survival-equipment instruction_status = completed; every crew member shall have personal_and_group_survival_equipment_training_status = completed.
requirements.requiredInputs: Passenger and crew manifests with instruction/training records
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Passengers shall be instructed in the use of the personal survival equipment and the action to take in an emergency; and the crew shall be trained in the use of the personal survival equipment and group survival equipment.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: emergency-ration capacity variables
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: available_emergency_ration_person_days >= persons_on_board * maximum_expected_rescue_time_days.
requirements.requiredInputs: Persons-on-board count, adopted rescue time, and ration capacity
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Adequate emergency rations shall be provided, for the maximum expected time of rescue.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: ice-information receiver, display and currency properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: ice_information_receiver_present = true AND ice_information_display_present = true AND displayed_ice_information_status = current for the operating area.
requirements.requiredInputs: Navigation equipment inventory and time-stamped ice-information feed
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Ships shall have means of receiving and displaying current information on ice conditions in the area of operation.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: construction date and echo-sounding equipment-count properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF construction_date >= '2017-01-01' AND ship_ice_strengthened = true, THEN independent_echo_sounding_device_count >= 2 OR (echo_sounding_device_count >= 1 AND independent_transducer_count >= 2).
requirements.requiredInputs: Construction date, ice-strengthening status, and echo-sounding equipment topology
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Ships constructed on or after 1 January 2017, ice strengthened in accordance with chapter 3, shall have either two independent echo-sounding devices or one echo-sounding device with two separate independent transducers.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: SOLAS compliance and bridge-visibility properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.encodingPattern: Cross-regulation compliance and conditional status constraint
requirements.normalizedRequirement: SOLAS_V_22_1_9_4_compliance_status = compliant AND, where required by bridge configuration, clear_view_astern_status = compliant.
requirements.requiredInputs: SOLAS compliance evidence, bridge configuration, and visibility assessment
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Ships shall comply with SOLAS regulation V/22.1.9.4, irrespective of the date of construction and the size and, depending on the bridge configuration, have a clear view astern.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: antenna and ice-prevention properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF ice_accretion_likely = true, THEN every required navigation or communication antenna shall have ice_accumulation_prevention_means_present = true.
requirements.requiredInputs: Antenna inventory, ice-accretion applicability, and prevention arrangement
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: For ships operating in areas and during periods where ice accretion is likely to occur, means to prevent the accumulation of ice on antennas required for navigation and communication shall be provided.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: below-hull sensor and ice-protection properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF required_sensor_projects_below_hull = true, THEN sensor_ice_protection_present = true.
requirements.requiredInputs: Required-sensor inventory, projection location, and ice protection
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Where equipment required by SOLAS chapter V or this chapter has sensors that project below the hull, such sensors shall be protected against ice.

requirements.anchorMapField: iceClass -> reg:iceClass; No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: ship_category, construction_date, bridge-wing properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF ship_category IN {'A','B'} AND construction_date >= '2017-01-01', THEN bridge_wings_enclosed = true OR bridge_wing_protection_design_status = approved.
requirements.requiredInputs: Ship category, construction date, and bridge-wing design evidence
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: In category A and B ships constructed on or after 1 January 2017, the bridge wings shall be enclosed or designed to protect navigational equipment and operating personnel.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: heading-means count, independence and power properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: non_magnetic_heading_means_count >= 2; the two means shall be independent and each shall be connected to main_power and emergency_power.
requirements.requiredInputs: Heading-equipment inventory, independence relation, and power connections
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Ships shall have two non-magnetic means to determine and display their heading. Both means shall be independent and shall be connected to the ship's main and emergency source of power.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: latitude and GNSS compass properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF planned_or_actual_latitude_deg > 80, THEN GNSS_compass_or_equivalent_count >= 1 AND connected_to_main_power = true AND connected_to_emergency_power = true.
requirements.requiredInputs: Voyage latitude, compass inventory, and power connections
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Ships proceeding to latitudes over 80 degrees shall be fitted with at least one GNSS compass or equivalent, which shall be connected to the ship's main and emergency source of power.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: daylight profile and visual-ice-detection equipment properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF solely_24_hour_daylight_operation = false, THEN (bridge_controlled_rotatable_narrow_beam_searchlight_count >= 2 AND searchlight_coverage_arc_deg >= 360) OR alternate_visual_ice_detection_means_approval_status = approved.
requirements.requiredInputs: Operating-light profile, searchlight inventory/coverage, and alternative approval evidence
requirements.section: Part I-A Chapter 9 - Additional navigational equipment
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Ships, with the exception of those solely operating in areas with 24 h daylight, shall be equipped with two remotely rotatable, narrow-beam search lights controllable from the bridge to provide lighting over an arc of 360 degrees, or other means to visually detect ice.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: escort stopped-light properties
requirements.canonicalVariables: icebreaker_escort_operation, stopped_light_present, manual_initiation, flashing_red, visible_from_astern, visibility_range_nm, COLREG_stern_light_arc_compliance_status
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF icebreaker_escort_operation = true, THEN manually_initiated_flashing_red_stopped_light_present = true, light_visible_from_astern = true, visibility_range_nm >= 2, and COLREG_stern_light_arc_compliance_status = compliant.
requirements.requiredInputs: Escort operating mode and stopped-light specifications/compliance evidence
requirements.section: Part I-A Chapter 9 - Additional navigational equipment
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Ships involved in operations with an icebreaker escort shall be equipped with a manually initiated flashing red light visible from astern to indicate when the ship is stopped. This light shall have a range of visibility of at least two nautical miles, and the horizontal and vertical arcs of visibility shall conform to the stern light specifications required by the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: route communication-coverage properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: For every point on the intended operating route, ship_to_ship_communication_available = true AND ship_to_shore_communication_available = true using voice and/or data.
requirements.requiredInputs: Intended route and communication coverage assessment
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Two-way voice and/or data communications ship-to-ship and ship-to-shore shall be available at all points along the intended operating routes.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: SAR communication capability properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: two_way_on_scene_communication_present = true AND SAR_coordination_communication_present = true AND aeronautical_frequency_capability_present = true.
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Means for two-way on-scene and SAR coordination communications for search and rescue purposes including aeronautical frequencies shall be provided.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: telemedical_assistance_communication_equipment_present
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: telemedical_assistance_communication_equipment_present = true.
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Appropriate communication equipment to enable telemedical assistance in polar areas shall be provided.

requirements.activeStatus: Evidence-only - physical result not inferred by SHACL
requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: survival-craft communication duration-test properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: Every mandatory survival-craft communication device shall have demonstrated_operating_duration_days >= maximum_expected_rescue_time_days AND duration_test_status = passed.
requirements.requiredInputs: Device inventory, duration-test records, and adopted rescue time
requirements.section: Part I-A Chapter 10 - Survival craft communications
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Mandatory communication equipment for use in survival craft, including liferafts and rescue boats, shall be capable of operation during the maximum expected time of rescue.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: escort sound-signaling properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF ship_provides_icebreaking_escort = true, THEN astern_facing_sound_signaling_system_present = true AND International_Code_of_Signals_compliance_status = compliant.
requirements.requiredInputs: Escort role, signaling-system installation, and code-compliance evidence
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Ships intended to provide icebreaking escort shall be equipped with a sound signaling system mounted to face astern to indicate escort and emergency manoeuvres to following ships as described in the International Code of Signals.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: SAR communication and supported-frequency properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: SAR_communication_capability shall include rescue_coordination_centre_voice_or_data = true AND aircraft_voice_frequency_support_MHz containing both 121.5 and 123.1.
requirements.requiredInputs: Communication capability declaration and supported frequency list
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Two-way on-scene and SAR coordination communication capability in ships shall include: voice and/or data communications with relevant rescue coordination centres; and equipment for voice communications with aircraft on 121.5 and 123.1 MHz.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: TMAS communication capability properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: TMAS_two_way_voice_capability = true AND TMAS_two_way_data_capability = true.
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: The communication equipment shall provide for two-way voice and data communication with a Telemedical Assistance Service (TMAS).

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: survival-craft communication-device counts
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF ship_operates_in_low_air_temperature = true, THEN every released rescue boat and lifeboat shall carry at least one ship-to-shore distress-alert device, one location-signal device, and one on-scene transmit/receive communication device.
requirements.requiredInputs: Operating-temperature class, craft inventory, and assigned device inventory
requirements.section: Part I-A Chapter 10 - Survival craft communications
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: For ships intended to operate in low air temperature, all rescue boats and lifeboats, whenever released for evacuation, shall: for distress alerting, carry one device for transmitting ship-to-shore alerts; in order to be located, carry one device for transmitting signals for location; and for on-scene communications, carry one device for transmitting and receiving on-scene communications.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: survival-craft communication-device counts
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF ship_operates_in_low_air_temperature = true, THEN every other survival craft shall carry at least one location-signal device and one on-scene transmit/receive communication device.
requirements.requiredInputs: Operating-temperature class, craft inventory, and assigned device inventory
requirements.section: Part I-A Chapter 10 - Survival craft communications
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: For ships intended to operate in low air temperature, all other survival craft shall: in order to be located, carry one device for transmitting signals for location; and for on-scene communications, carry one device for transmitting and receiving on-scene communications.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: battery-life procedure and device-availability properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: battery_life_management_procedure_present = true AND procedure_implementation_status = active AND every mandatory survival-craft communication device shall remain available for maximum_expected_rescue_time_days.
requirements.requiredInputs: Implemented procedure, device inventory, battery/availability assessment, and rescue time
requirements.section: Part I-A Chapter 10 - Survival craft communications
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Recognizing the limitations arising from battery life, procedures shall be developed and implemented such that mandatory communication equipment for use in survival craft, including liferafts and rescue boats, are available for operation during the maximum expected time of rescue.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: voyage plan and hazard-coverage properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: voyage_plan_present = true AND every identified_intended_voyage_hazard shall be addressed by the voyage plan.
requirements.requiredInputs: Voyage plan and intended-voyage hazard register
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: The voyage plan shall take into account the potential hazards of the intended voyage.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: polar_route_plan and voyage-planning topic-coverage properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: The polar-route planning record shall cover all nine clause 11.3 topics: PWOM procedures, hydrographic/navigation limitations, current ice/iceberg information, historical ice/temperature data, places of refuge, marine-mammal measures, routing/speed/VTS information, protected areas, and remoteness from SAR.
requirements.requiredInputs: Route planning record and nine required topic indicators
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: The master shall consider a route through polar waters, taking into account the following: the procedures required by the PWOM; any limitations of the hydrographic information and aids to navigation available; current information on the extent and type of ice and icebergs in the vicinity of the intended route; statistical information on ice and temperatures from former years; places of refuge; current information and measures to be taken when marine mammals are encountered, relating to known areas with densities of marine mammals, including seasonal migration areas; current information on relevant ships' routing systems, speed recommendations and vessel traffic services relating to known areas with densities of marine mammals, including seasonal migration areas; national and international designated protected areas along the route; and operation in areas remote from SAR capabilities.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: ice condition, crew role and training-level properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: Required polar training level shall be derived from ice_condition, ship_type, and crew_role according to the clause 12.3.1 matrix, and each applicable crew member shall have a valid matching STCW qualification.
requirements.requiredInputs: Ice condition, ship type, crew manifest, and STCW credentials
requirements.section: Part I-A Chapter 12 - Manning and training
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: In order to meet the functional requirement of paragraph 12.2 above while operating in polar waters, masters, chief mates and officers in charge of a navigational watch shall be qualified in accordance with chapter V of the STCW Convention and the STCW Code, as amended, as follows: Ice conditions | Tankers | Passenger ships | Other. Ice free | Not applicable. | Not applicable. | Not applicable. Open waters | Basic training for master, chief mate and officers in charge of a navigational watch. | Basic training for master, chief mate and officers in charge of a navigational watch. | Not applicable. Other waters | Advanced training for master and chief mate. Basic training for officers in charge of a navigational watch. | Advanced training for master and chief mate. Basic training for officers in charge of a navigational watch. | Advanced training for master and chief mate. Basic training for officers in charge of a navigational watch.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: alternate-person permission and credential/coverage properties
requirements.canonicalVariables: alternate_qualified_person_used, administration_permission_status, STCW_II_2_status, STCW_A_II_2_status, advanced_polar_training_status, watch_coverage_status, rest_compliance_status, ice_condition, ice_concentration_tenths, designated_officer_basic_training_status
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF alternate_qualified_person_used = true, THEN administration_permission_status = approved and all five conditions in clause 12.3.2 shall be satisfied, including STCW II/2 and A-II/2 certification, advanced polar training, watch coverage, rest compliance, and the condition-specific basic-training safeguards for designated officers.
requirements.requiredInputs: Administration permission, credentials, watch schedule, rest records, and operating ice condition
requirements.section: Part I-A Chapter 12 - Manning and training
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: The Administration may allow the use of a person(s) other than the master, chief mate or officers of the navigational watch to satisfy the requirements for training, provided that: this person(s) shall be qualified and certified in accordance with regulation II/2 of the STCW Convention and section A-II/2 of the STCW Code, and meet the advance training requirements set out in the table in paragraph 12.3.1; while operating in polar waters the ship carries a sufficient number of persons meeting the appropriate training requirements for polar waters to cover all watches; this person(s) is subject to the Administration's minimum hours of rest requirements at all times; when operating in waters other than open waters or bergy waters, the master, chief mate and officers in charge of a navigational watch on passenger ships and tankers shall meet the applicable basic training requirements set out in the table in paragraph 12.3.1; and when operating in waters with an ice concentration of more than 2/10, the master, chief mate and officers in charge of a navigational watch on cargo ships other than tankers shall meet the applicable basic training requirements set out in the table in paragraph 12.3.1.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: crew duty and PWOM familiarization properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: Every crew member shall have PWOM_familiarization_status = completed for all procedures and equipment relevant to assigned_duties.
requirements.requiredInputs: Crew manifest, duty assignments, PWOM relevance mapping, and familiarization records
requirements.section: Part I-A Chapter 12 - Manning and training
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Every crew member shall be made familiar with the procedures and equipment contained or referenced in the PWOM relevant to their assigned duties.

requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: In Arctic waters any discharge into the sea of oil or oily mixtures from any ship shall be prohibited.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: discharged_material_type and prohibition-applicability properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF discharged_material_type IN {clean_ballast, segregated_ballast}, THEN clause_1_1_1_oil_discharge_prohibition_applicable = false.
requirements.section: Part II-A Chapter 1 - Prevention of pollution by oil
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: The provisions of paragraph 1.1.1 shall not apply to the discharge of clean or segregated ballast.

requirements.anchorMapField: No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: polar-operation coverage in MARPOL documents
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015

requirements.requiredInputs: Applicable MARPOL documents and polar-operation coverage indicators
requirements.section: Part II-A Chapter 1 - Prevention of pollution by oil
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: Operation in polar waters shall be taken into account, as appropriate, in the Oil Record Books, manuals and the shipboard oil pollution emergency plan or the shipboard marine pollution emergency plan as required by MARPOL Annex I.

requirements.anchorMapField: iceClass -> reg:iceClass; No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: oil-fuel tank capacity and separation variables
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF ship_category IN {'A','B'} AND construction_date >= '2017-01-01' AND aggregate_oil_fuel_capacity_m3 < 600 AND individual_oil_fuel_tank_capacity_m3 > 30, THEN oil_fuel_tank_outer_shell_separation_m >= 0.76.
requirements.requiredInputs: Ship category/date and oil-fuel tank capacities/separation measurements
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: For category A and B ships constructed on or after 1 January 2017 with an aggregate oil fuel capacity of less than 600 m^3, all oil fuel tanks shall be separated from the outer shell by a distance of not less than 0.76 m. This provision does not apply to small oil fuel tanks with a maximum individual capacity not greater than 30 m^3.

requirements.anchorMapField: iceClass -> reg:iceClass; No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: cargo-tank oil-service and separation variables
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF ship_category IN {'A','B'} AND ship_type != oil_tanker AND construction_date >= '2017-01-01' AND cargo_tank_carries_oil = true, THEN cargo_tank_outer_shell_separation_m >= 0.76.
requirements.requiredInputs: Ship category/type/date and cargo-tank use/separation measurements
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: For category A and B ships other than oil tankers constructed on or after 1 January 2017, all cargo tanks constructed and utilized to carry oil shall be separated from the outer shell by a distance of not less than 0.76 m.

requirements.anchorMapField: iceClass -> reg:iceClass; No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: deadweight and cargo-tank protection-compliance properties
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF ship_category IN {'A','B'} AND ship_type = oil_tanker AND deadweight_tonnes < 5000 AND construction_date >= '2017-01-01', THEN entire_cargo_tank_length_double_bottom_protection_status = compliant with MARPOL I/19.6.1 AND wing_tank_protection_status = compliant with MARPOL I/19.3.1 and I/19.6.2.
requirements.requiredInputs: Ship particulars, protection arrangement, and linked MARPOL compliance evidence
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: For category A and B oil tankers of less than 5,000 tonnes deadweight constructed on or after 1 January 2017, the entire cargo tank length shall be protected with: double bottom tanks or spaces complying with the applicable requirements of regulation 19.6.1 of MARPOL Annex I; and wing tanks or spaces arranged in accordance with regulation 19.3.1 of MARPOL Annex I and complying with the applicable requirements for distance referred to in regulation 19.6.2 of MARPOL Annex I.

requirements.anchorMapField: iceClass -> reg:iceClass; No direct AnchorMap term found; propose code-safe alias: tank type, capacity and separation variables
requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
requirements.normalizedRequirement: IF ship_category IN {'A','B'} AND construction_date >= '2017-01-01' AND tank_type IN {oil_residue_tank, oily_bilge_water_holding_tank} AND individual_tank_capacity_m3 > 30, THEN tank_outer_shell_separation_m >= 0.76.
requirements.requiredInputs: Ship category/date and tank inventory/capacity/separation measurements
requirements.source: International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (Polar Code)
requirements.sourceText: For category A and B ships constructed on or after 1 January 2017 all oil residue (sludge) tanks and oily bilge water holding tanks shall be separated from the outer shell by a distance of not less than 0.76 m. This provision does not apply to small tanks with a maximum individual capacity not greater than 30 m^3.

requirements.edition: Resolution MSC.385(94), adopted 21 Nov 2014; consolidated with MEPC.264(68), adopted 15 May 2015
